summary: The shared shadow predicate excluded protocol_members wholesale, so a Protocol body's `def x` failed to shadow an inherited class attribute and `C.x` folded the base's constant instead of CPython's function object.
note: Confirmed by measurement before fixing: for `class P(Protocol): def x(self) -> int: ...` / `class A: x: int = 2` / `class C(P, A)`, CPython printed the function object while pycc printed 2. Both crates agreed on the wrong value, so the shared-predicate guard could not catch it. The exclusion is narrowed to ProtocolMember::Attribute; ProtocolMember::Method now shadows and the read stays T0044. Pinned by tests/issue_974_inherited_class_attr_by_class_name.rs::a_protocol_method_member_shadows_an_inherited_class_attribute; the pre-existing positive test was renamed to name its Attribute half.

summary: The #974 sentence listed four of the five shadow namespaces the predicate checks, omitting enum members, while docs/TYPE_SYSTEM.md listed all of them.
note: The sentence now lists methods, @staticmethod, @classmethod, @property, enum members and a Protocol-body def. The explanatory prose was deliberately not added: docs/ROADMAP.md had 81 bytes of headroom under scripts/check-site.sh's 168960-byte llms.txt budget, and the owning specification docs/TYPE_SYSTEM.md carries the reasoning.

summary: The class-name read bullet described the MRO walk unconditionally, without disclosing that a PEP 695 generic class accepts the read under `pycc check` and then fails `pycc build` with T0021.
note: The divergence predates #974 (an own-declared class attribute on a generic class already diverged the same way) and is item 3 of follow-up issue #989, which is why this change's test matrix carries no PEP 695 case. The bullet now states the exception inline and cites #989.
